ENFORCEMENT RULES OF THE ACT CONCERNING THE CONTRACTING OUT OF POST OFFICE COUNTER OPERATIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) These Rules prescribe the matters delegated under the Act Concerning the Contracting Out of Post Office Counter Operations and its Enforcement Decree, together with the matters necessary for their implementation.

Article 2 (Islands and Remote Districts Where Postal Savings Services May Be Contracted Out) The "islands and remote districts specified by Ordinance of the Ministry of Science and ICT" in Article 3 (2) 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act Concerning the Contracting Out of Post Office Counter Operations (hereinafter the "Decree") mean islands or remote districts where no cooperative within the meaning of Article 2, subparagraph 1, of the Agricultural Cooperatives Act has been established. <Amended March 24, 2013, and July 26, 2017>

Article 3 (Public Announcement of Recruitment of Prospective Contractors) If the head of a Regional Postal Administration intends to contract out post office counter operations under Article 3 of the Act Concerning the Contracting Out of Post Office Counter Operations (hereinafter the "Act"), the head must publish an invitation for applicants in the Official Gazette, on the Internet, and by other suitable means no later than 15 days before the first day on which applications are accepted under a plan made pursuant to Article 6 of the Decree. The announcement shall include: <Amended December 31, 2014>
1. The area where the post office or postal service office providing the contracted services (hereinafter a "contracted post office") is proposed to be established;
2. The period for accepting applications;
3. The place where application forms may be obtained and submitted;
4. The date of the announcement under Article 5 (2);
5. Other matters needed for applying to operate post office counter services under contract.

Article 4 (Applications to Receive Outsourced Operations)
(1) A person seeking to receive post office counter operations under Article 3 of the Act (hereinafter an "applicant") must submit two copies of the application for outsourced post office counter services, in the attached Form No. 1 (including an electronic document; hereinafter the "application"), with the documents listed below according to the relevant category. Such documents may be electronic and must have been issued or prepared after the announcement under Article 3. The application shall be submitted to the head of the Regional Postal Administration through the post office having jurisdiction over the area whose head holds a government rank of Grade 5 or higher (hereinafter the "jurisdictional post office"). However, where the applicant requests permission under Article 16 to use the building and facilities of a post office that has been closed, the documents under subparagraph 1 (a) and (b), or subparagraph 2 (b) through (d), need not be attached. <Amended December 31, 2014>
1. Applicants falling within Article 3 (2) 1 or 2 of the Act:
(a) A sketch map showing the location for establishing the contracted post office;
(b) A floor plan of the office intended for use as the contracted post office.
2. Applicants falling within any of Article 3 (2) 3 through 6 of the Act:
(a) Documents proving that the applicant meets any of the requirements of Article 3 (2) 3 through 6 of the Act;
(b) A sketch map of the location for the contracted post office;
(c) A floor plan of the premises intended for use as the contracted post office;
(d) If the office is leased, a copy of the lease agreement;
(e) Deleted. <December 5, 2024>
(2) The responsible public official receiving an application shall verify the following information through the shared administrative information system under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act. However, if the applicant declines to consent to verification of the document under subparagraph 2, the applicant must attach that document. <Amended December 5, 2024>
1. Certificate of registration of a corporation, applicable only if the applicant is a corporation;
2. Certificate of business registration that excludes the resident registration number;
3. Certificate showing the registered particulars of the building where the contracted post office is to be established, applicable only to applications submitted under paragraph (1) 2.

Article 5 (Selection and Announcement of Prospective Contractors)
(1) Upon receiving an application under Article 4, the head of the jurisdictional post office must inspect whether the proposed location is suitable for establishing a contracted post office and forward the application to the competent head of the Regional Postal Administration with a written opinion on the suitability of the site. <Amended December 31, 2014>
(2) Upon receiving the application and the opinion under paragraph (1), the competent head of the Regional Postal Administration must select a prospective contractor pursuant to Article 4 (2) of the Act and Article 7 of the Decree, and publicly announce: <Amended December 31, 2014>
1. The names of the prospective contractors;
2. How and by when the security deposit, guarantee insurance certificate, or financial guarantee certificate must be paid or presented;
3. The expected date for concluding the agreement for operating post office counter services (hereinafter the "contract for outsourced operations");
4. Other matters necessary for concluding that contract.

Article 6 (Payment of Deposits and Provision of Security)
(1) A person who has concluded a contract under Article 4 (3) of the Act (hereinafter a "contractor") and is required to pay a security deposit under Article 8 (1) of the Decree shall pay it to the jurisdictional post office, obtain confirmation from the head of that post office on the deposit payment form in attached Form No. 2, and submit the confirmed form to the competent head of the Regional Postal Administration. The head of the jurisdictional post office shall place the deposit in a post office fixed-term savings account. <Amended May 30, 2011>
(2) A contractor who submits a guarantee insurance certificate pursuant to Article 8 (1) of the Decree must enter into an insurance contract satisfying all the following requirements with an insurance company and submit the guarantee insurance certificate to the competent head of the Regional Postal Administration: <Amended May 30, 2011>
1. The contractor is the policyholder;
2. The head of the competent Regional Postal Administration is the insured party;
3. The insurance period is three years;
4. The place designated for payment of insurance proceeds is the location of the competent Regional Postal Administration.
(3) A contractor presenting a financial guarantee certificate under Article 8 (1) of the Decree must submit it to the competent head of the Regional Postal Administration with:
1. A certificate of the financial guarantor's property;
2. A copy of an identity document issued by a public authority, such as a resident identification card.
[The Korean source edition contains damaged characters within the fourth requirement of paragraph (2); its surrounding wording establishes that the requirement concerns the location for payment of the insurance amount.]

Article 7 (Conclusion of the Contract) The contract for outsourced operations is formed when a person selected as prospective contractor under Article 5 (2) submits an offer together with a contract document accompanied by the deposit payment form, guarantee insurance certificate, or financial guarantee certificate required under Article 6, and the head of the competent Regional Postal Administration accepts that offer. <Amended December 31, 2014>

Article 8 (Custody and Management of Deposit and Guarantee Documents) Deposit payment forms, guarantee insurance certificates, and financial guarantee certificates submitted by contractors under Article 6 shall be kept by the head of the competent Regional Postal Administration or the head of the jurisdictional post office. <Amended December 31, 2014>

Article 9 (Inquiry into the Qualification of Financial Guarantors)
(1) After receiving a financial guarantee certificate under Article 6 (3), the head of the Regional Postal Administration must inquire at the institution issuing the guarantor's property certificate at least once each year to verify the guarantor's financial condition and related matters. <Amended December 31, 2014>
(2) If, following the inquiry under paragraph (1), the head considers the guarantor no longer suitable because of a change in financial status or another circumstance, the head must immediately require the contractor to replace the guarantor or provide alternative security. <Amended December 31, 2014>

Article 10 (Interest on Deposits) When returning a security deposit paid pursuant to Article 6 (1), the competent head of the Regional Postal Administration must add interest calculated for the period from the day following the deposit payment date to the date of return, at the interest rate applicable to post office fixed-term savings deposits at the time the security deposit was originally paid. <Amended December 31, 2014>

Article 11 (Standards for Facilities and Equipment)
(1) Facilities at a contracted post office under Article 6 (2) of the Act must meet or exceed the standards established by the competent head of the Regional Postal Administration in consideration of the volume of operations handled there. <Amended December 31, 2014>
(2) At least seven days before starting post office counter operations, the contractor must have the following equipment:
1. A secure storage box for specially handled postal items;
2. A storage box for postal stamps and related items;
3. A storage box for parcel post;
4. Other equipment or facilities that the President of Korea Post considers necessary and requests.

Article 12 (Hours for Performing Outsourced Operations)
(1) The hours for outsourced operations at a contracted post office under Article 7 of the Act, excluding the receipt and disbursement of National Treasury funds and cash, shall be determined and publicly announced by the competent head of the Regional Postal Administration, taking into account the level of public use and setting at least 20 hours per week. <Amended December 31, 2014, and February 21, 2020>
(2) The hours for receiving and disbursing National Treasury funds and cash at contracted post offices shall follow the cash-handling hours of ordinary post office counters.
(3) Holidays at contracted post offices shall follow the Regulation on Public Holidays for Government Offices. However, if the competent head of the Regional Postal Administration considers it particularly necessary for user convenience, the head may require services to be performed on a public holiday or change the holiday schedule. <Amended December 31, 2014>

Article 13 (Operating Methods and Procedures for Outsourced Operations)
(1) The contractor must display at the contracted post office:
1. The certificate of assignment of post office counter operations;
2. The schedule of postal rates;
3. The schedule of hours when post office counter operations are available;
4. Other matters that the President of Korea Post considers necessary and requests.
(2) In performing outsourced operations, the contractor must comply with the contract and applicable laws and regulations.
(3) Matters of operating methods and procedures not governed by paragraphs (1) and (2) shall follow the methods and procedures for ordinary post office operations as determined by the President of Korea Post.

Article 14 (Commissions for Outsourced Operations)
(1) The President of Korea Post shall pay the contractor commissions under Article 11 (2) of the Act for the following outsourced operations:
1. Acceptance of domestically mailed items requiring special handling;
2. Acceptance of internationally mailed items requiring special handling;
3. Issuance and payment of postal money orders;
4. Deposits and payments through the postal giro system, including collection of National Treasury funds and public utility charges;
5. Acceptance of mail without affixed postage stamps, including bulk-paid and deferred-payment mail;
6. Postal savings and postal insurance operations;
7. Operations contracted out pursuant to Article 2, subparagraph 2, of the Decree.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the President of Korea Post may withhold commissions for outsourced operations performed outside the areas designated for those operations under Article 6 (1) of the Act.
(3) The commissions under paragraph (1) shall be determined and publicly announced by the President of Korea Post.

Article 15 (Government-Supplied Goods)
(1) Under Article 12 of the Act, the President of Korea Post may provide a contractor with the following goods at government expense or allow the contractor to use them without charge: <Amended February 21, 2020>
1. Official stamps and seals for operations;
2. Weighing scales;
3. Date stamps and movable type;
4. Equipment for printing amounts when issuing money orders;
5. A safe;
6. Deleted. <February 21, 2020>
7. Consumable supplies for postal information-processing systems;
8. Other items deemed necessary by the President of Korea Post.
(2) The contractor must use the government-provided goods under paragraph (1) while performing outsourced operations.
(3) The contractor must exercise the care of a prudent manager in keeping and managing goods supplied under Article 12 of the Act and shall neither transfer them nor lend them to another person.
(4) On termination of the contract for outsourced operations, the contractor must return the goods provided.

Article 16 (Permission to Use Buildings and Facilities of Post Offices) When necessary for contracting out post office counter operations under Article 3 of the Act, the President of Korea Post may permit a contractor to use the building and facilities of a closed post office pursuant to Article 20 of the Special Act on the Operation of Postal Services.

These Rules take effect on the day of their promulgation.

ADDENDA (Enforcement Rules of the Organization of the Ministry of Knowledge Economy and Its Affiliated Agencies) <Ordinance No. 187, May 30, 2011>

Article 2 (Amendment of Other Regulations)
Paragraphs (1) and (2) omitted.
Paragraph (3): The Enforcement Rules of the Act Concerning the Contracting Out of Post Office Counter Operations are partially amended as follows:
In the main text of Article 6 (1), in Article 6 (2) before the subparagraphs and in its subparagraph 2, each reference to "Head of the Postal Administration" is replaced with "Head of the Regional Postal Administration"; in Article 6 (2), subparagraph 4, "Postal Administration" is replaced with "Regional Postal Administration"; and in Article 6 (3) in the text preceding its subparagraphs, "Head of the Postal Administration" is replaced with "Head of the Regional Postal Administration".

Articles 2 through 5 omitted.

Paragraphs (1) through (23) omitted.

In Article 2, "Ordinance of the Ministry of Knowledge Economy" is replaced with "Ordinance of the Ministry of Science, ICT and Future Planning".
Paragraphs (25) through (31) omitted.

In Article 2, "Ordinance of the Ministry of Science, ICT and Future Planning" is replaced with "Ordinance of the Ministry of Science and ICT".
Paragraphs (29) through (41) omitted.

ADDENDA <Ordinance No. 40, February 21, 2020>
Article 1 (Entry into force) These Rules take effect on promulgation.

APPLICATION DECLARATION

Pursuant to Article 3 of the Act Concerning the Contracting Out of Post Office Counter Operations and Article 4 of its Enforcement Rules, I hereby apply to operate the post office counter services on an outsourced basis as stated above.

Applicant: __________________________  (Signature or seal)

To: Head of the Regional Postal Administration

DOCUMENTS TO BE SUBMITTED BY THE APPLICANT (REPRESENTATIVE)

Applicants falling under Article 3 (2) 1 or 2 of the Act:
1. A sketch map showing the proposed location of the post office to be operated under contract.
2. A floor plan of the office proposed for use as the contracted post office.

Applicants falling under any of Article 3 (2) 3 through 6 of the Act:
1. Documents establishing that the applicant is a person qualifying under any of Article 3 (2) 3 through 6 of the Act.
2. A sketch map showing the proposed location of the post office to be operated under contract.
3. A floor plan of the office proposed for use as the contracted post office.
4. If the office intended for use as the contracted post office is leased: a copy of the lease agreement.

Application fee: None.

MATTERS TO BE VERIFIED BY THE RESPONSIBLE PUBLIC OFFICIAL

1. Certificate of corporate registration (only where the applicant is a corporation).
2. Certificate of business registration (meaning a business registration certificate with the resident registration number omitted; the same meaning applies throughout this form).
3. Certificate of registered particulars of the building intended for use as the contracted post office (only where an application under Article 4 (1) 2 of the Enforcement Rules of the Act Concerning the Contracting Out of Post Office Counter Operations is received).

CONSENT TO JOINT USE OF ADMINISTRATIVE INFORMATION

I consent to verification of my business registration certificate through the shared use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act in connection with the processing of this application.

* If the applicant does not consent, the applicant must submit the relevant document directly.

| 1 | Preparation of application | Applicant |
| 2 | Receipt of application | Processing institution — Post office having jurisdiction |
| 3 | Examination and review | Processing institution — Regional Postal Administration |
| 4 | Conclusion of contract for outsourced operations | Processing institution — Regional Postal Administration |

Form size: 210 mm × 297 mm; ordinary paper, 80 g/m².
